diagnosis.finding: Not a harness code defect. Screening decode_timeout_seconds is fitted per-record (8.0s here, well under the thrash-calibrated <=12.0s test ceiling); the scoreboard's effective_decode_timeout_seconds_min/max reports the whole-chunk budget (8.0 x decode_batch_size_max=3 = 24.0), which was initially misread as a per-record timeout during triage. The component-plan recipe's compiler_ms_mean (~23.3s) is genuinely right at that 24s chunk budget on this container's CPU throughput -- a capacity edge, not a regression: this exact recipe family completed near-identical latencies (p50 18.3-23.1s) in the 2026-08-03 c2 run without a code change in between.
diagnosis.action_taken: Added a clarifying comment at the effective_decode_timeout_seconds_min/max computation in eval_runner.py and a pinned regression test (test_screening_chunk_timeout_is_per_chunk_not_per_record) locking in the exact decode_timeout_seconds=8.0/chunk=3 -> 24.0 scenario, to prevent future misdiagnosis of chunk-level totals as per-record timeouts. No timeout value, gate, or budget was loosened.
